title: Trash
why: Files you already threw away. They use space until the Trash is emptied, and emptying it can't be undone.

title: Homebrew downloads
why: Packages Homebrew already installed, and old versions of them. Add -n to the command to see what would go.

title: uv cache
why: Python packages uv downloaded. It fetches them again when a project needs them.

title: pip cache
why: Python packages pip downloaded. It fetches them again when needed.

title: npm cache
why: Packages npm downloaded. It fetches them again when needed.

title: Yarn cache
why: Packages Yarn downloaded. It fetches them again when needed.

title: pnpm store
why: Removes the packages no project uses any more.

title: Go build cache
why: Compiled Go code. The next build takes longer and fills it again.

title: Go modules
why: Downloaded Go dependencies. They come back the next time a project needs them.

title: CocoaPods cache
why: Pods already downloaded. CocoaPods fetches them again when needed.

title: Conda packages
why: Package archives and caches. Your environments keep working.

title: Composer cache
why: PHP packages Composer downloaded. It fetches them again when needed.

title: Dart and Flutter packages
why: Downloaded packages. Run pub get in your projects afterwards to fetch what they need.

title: Rust downloads
why: Crates Cargo downloaded. It fetches them again on the next build.

title: Gradle caches
why: Dependencies and build results. The next build is slower while Gradle fetches them again. Stop any running builds first.

title: Swift Package Manager cache
why: Downloaded Swift packages. They come back on the next build.

title: Carthage cache
why: Downloaded dependencies. They come back the next time they are needed.

title: Bazel build output
why: Everything Bazel built. The next build starts from scratch.

title: Xcode build data
why: Build results and indexes. Xcode makes them again, so the next build of each project takes longer.

title: Xcode cache
why: Temporary data of Xcode. Quit Xcode first.

title: Device support files
why: Debugging symbols copied from devices. Xcode copies them again when you connect one.

title: Simulator caches
why: Temporary data of the simulators. They rebuild it when they start.

title: Browsers for testing
why: Browsers that testing tools downloaded. They download them again when needed.

title: Electron downloads
why: Files build tools downloaded. They download them again when needed.

title: Web browser caches
why: Copies of web pages. Sites load a little slower at first, and you stay logged in. Quit the browser first.

title: Visual Studio Code caches
why: Temporary data of the editor. Quit it first.

title: Adobe media cache
why: Previews of media files. Adobe apps make them again when you open a project.

title: iPhone and iPad updates
why: System updates already downloaded for your devices. Your Mac downloads them again if needed.

title: Mail attachments opened
why: Copies of attachments you opened. The originals stay in your messages.

title: Logs
why: Records of what apps did, useful only for tracking down a problem. Apps start new ones.

title: App caches
why: Temporary data of your apps, which they make again. Some may be slower for a while. Quit them first.

title: Caches inside app data
why: Temporary data of apps like Slack or Discord. Their own folders hold other things, so check the list, and quit those apps first.

title: Old temporary files
why: Left behind by apps, and unchanged for a week. macOS clears much of this when it restarts, which is the gentlest way to get rid of it.

title: Old installers in Downloads
why: Installers usually have no use once the app is installed. These are at least a month old.

title: macOS installers
why: Full copies of macOS. You can download them again from Apple.

title: node_modules in old projects
why: Project dependencies, unchanged for three months. Running npm install brings them back.

title: Xcode archives
why: Builds of your apps. Keep the ones you shipped, since they are needed to read crash reports.

title: Simulators
why: Removes the simulators for system versions no longer installed. The others stay.

title: Android emulators
why: Virtual devices and their data. You can create them again in Android Studio.

title: Docker
why: Removes stopped containers, unused networks and dangling images. Run docker system df first to see what takes up the space.

title: Maven repository
why: Downloaded dependencies. Anything you installed there yourself would have to be built again.

title: Hugging Face models
why: Downloaded models. They can be large to download again.

title: Ollama models
why: Downloaded models. The command lists them, and ollama rm removes the ones you no longer use.

title: Vagrant boxes
why: Removes old versions of the boxes you installed.

title: iPhone and iPad backups
why: These may be the only copy of what was on a device. Manage them in the Finder, with the device connected.
